sourceNote: Provider x credential-family taxonomy (issue #502). Grounded in benchmarks/lib/assessment.ts contract review text and benchmarks/detectors.json; every entry with an empty detectors list carries a source or note explaining why it is not detector-covered. Consumed by A2 (#503) and A3 (#504); zero-detector families default to `unsupported` in A8's support-matrix.json (#509), while an explicit supportStatus records a reviewed pending disposition.

families.name: IAM user access key
families.description: Long-term access key ID for an IAM user, prefixed AKIA.

families.name: STS temporary access key
families.description: Short-lived access key ID issued by AWS STS, prefixed ASIA; requires an accompanying session token.
families.note: aws-access-key's pattern is anchored to AKIA only (benchmarks/lib/assessment.ts contract), so ASIA values are not matched. classifyFixture already special-cases a bare AWS positive as policy, not must-redact, because "some legacy ASIA values also use digits outside the base32 alphabet".

families.name: STS service bearer token
families.description: AWS STS service-issued bearer credential, prefixed ABIA.
families.note: Documented in the same IAM unique-identifier prefix table as AKIA/ASIA; not matched by the AKIA-only pattern.

families.name: Context-specific credential
families.description: Context-specific temporary credential, prefixed ACCA.
families.note: Documented in the same IAM unique-identifier prefix table as AKIA/ASIA; not matched by the AKIA-only pattern.

families.name: IAM user secret access key
families.description: The 40-character secret paired with an IAM user access key ID. Has no distinguishing prefix or lexical marker.
families.note: The aws-access-key contract's companion field states a separate 40-character secret access key is required alongside the access key ID; this project has no dedicated detector for the secret half, which carries no stable prefix to anchor on.

families.name: OAuth access token
families.description: OAuth app access token, prefixed gho_.

families.name: GitHub App user-to-server token
families.description: GitHub App user-to-server token, prefixed ghu_.

families.name: GitHub App server-to-server token
families.description: GitHub App installation (server-to-server) token, prefixed ghs_.

families.name: Fine-grained personal access token
families.description: Repository- and permission-scoped PAT, prefixed github_pat_.
families.note: Named explicitly in issue #502 as a family the github-token detector does not cover: its pattern only matches the ghp_/gho_/ghu_/ghs_/ghr_ underscore-plus-36-character-body shape, which github_pat_ does not fit. Measured as the Beta.8 arrival family github-fine-grained-pat (#211, research #223): only the github_pat_ prefix is provider-documented; the 22 + _ + 59 body is community/tool evidence kept provisional, with no checksum or fixed 11 lead claimed. Scored as the arrival family github-fine-grained-pat (#730; docs/decisions/2026-09-24-score-arrival-families-by-finding-type.md): the product types it inside the shared github-token detector as github_fine_grained_personal_access_token, so its findings carry the arrival id and its status comes from its own contract, profile and ledger rows. github-fine-grained-pat is not a registry detector id.

families.name: Legacy personal access token
families.description: Legacy-format PAT, prefixed glpat- with a 20-character body.

families.name: Routable personal access token
families.description: Newer routable PAT format described on the same token-prefix page.
families.note: gitlab-token's contract review states explicitly that routable tokens are not covered by the 20-character-body pattern.

sources: benchmarks/lib/assessment.ts (classifyFixture variant guard: "Variant support must not be inferred from a related family name.")
families.note: classifyFixture explicitly routes sk_org_ values to "this variant needs a separate format contract; related detector support is not evidence of parity", so it is not claimed by stripe-token's live/test secret-key pattern.

sources: benchmarks/lib/assessment.ts (classifyFixture variant guard: "Variant support must not be inferred from a related family name.")
families.note: Same classifyFixture guard as the organization API key covers whsec_ values; stripe-token's pattern does not match them. Measured as the context-gated Beta.8 arrival family stripe-webhook-signing-secret (#211, research #224): Stripe documents the whsec_ prefix only; the body width and alphabet stay provisional (32 alphanumerics is a provider example, not a grammar; Stripe's own scrubber admits + / =). Scored as the arrival family stripe-webhook-signing-secret (#730; docs/decisions/2026-09-24-score-arrival-families-by-finding-type.md): the product types it inside the shared stripe-token detector as stripe_webhook_signing_secret, so its findings carry the arrival id and its status comes from its own contract, profile and ledger rows. stripe-webhook-signing-secret is not a registry detector id.

families.description: User OAuth token, prefixed xoxp-.
families.note: slack-token's contract lists xoxp- among the provider-documented prefixes but its pattern only matches xoxb-. Scored as the arrival family slack-user-token (#730; docs/decisions/2026-09-24-score-arrival-families-by-finding-type.md): the product types it inside the shared slack-token detector as slack_user_token, so its findings carry the arrival id and its status comes from its own contract, profile and ledger rows. slack-user-token is not a registry detector id.

families.name: App-level token

families.note: Documented alongside xoxb- in the same provider prefix table; not matched by the bot-token-only pattern. Measured as the Beta.8 arrival family slack-app-level-token (#211, research #222): only the xapp- prefix is provider-documented; section widths and alphabet are tool-only and contradictory (4-section 97-character vs Nosey Parker's 2-section 42-character) and stay unresolved. Scored as the arrival family slack-app-level-token (#730; docs/decisions/2026-09-24-score-arrival-families-by-finding-type.md): the product types it inside the shared slack-token detector as slack_app_level_token, so its findings carry the arrival id and its status comes from its own contract, profile and ledger rows. slack-app-level-token is not a registry detector id.

families.name: Project secret key
families.description: Project-scoped secret API key, prefixed sb_secret_.
families.note: supabase-token's contract is T1 since #207 (research #231): Supabase's self-hosting page documents sb_secret_ + 22-character random part + _ + 8-character checksum and says hosted keys use the same format; the base64url alphabet and the sha256 checksum are provider code only. The older 40-alphanumeric detector-coverage positives predate that grammar and are retained as policy regressions.

families.name: Personal access token
families.description: Management-API personal access token, prefixed sbp_/sbp_v0_.
families.note: #81 backfilled the supabase-management-token detector (redact-secret#535). Deliberately independent of supabase:secret-key's evidence, per https://github.com/redact-secret/redact-secret/blob/de6add470321f40d7b1cb36808d9f4559e6c2e99/docs/decisions/2026-09-20-scope-supabase-management-token-and-secret-key-independence.md.

families.name: Compatibility aggregate (unreviewed Vercel token shapes)
families.description: Legacy benchmark routing for the runtime vercel-token detector; not a modern credential-family support claim.
families.note: Bounded by product #858 and benchmark #373. This row preserves the existing aggregate detector/fixture routing while runtime behavior and finding types remain unchanged. Its T0 profile cells combine five implementation hypotheses and must not be copied to, or read as evidence for, any modern Vercel credential family. Opaque unprefixed examples are also outside the modern positive contract.

families.name: Personal access token
families.description: Modern personal access token identified by the provider-documented vcp_ marker.
families.note: Product #858 records this semantic contract as pending/T0. The class and vcp_ marker are provider-backed, but no reviewed source establishes a complete body grammar or boundary. The REST response's unprefixed bearerToken example beside prefix metadata remains unresolved. No scored fixture/profile cells exist, and the aggregate vercel-token detector is not attributed to this family.

families.name: Integration token
families.description: Modern integration token identified only by the provider-documented vci stem.
families.note: Product #858 records this semantic contract as pending/T0. Provider evidence establishes the vci stem but not the underscore, body grammar, or boundary; the current detector's vci_ branch is an implementation hypothesis. No scored fixture/profile cells exist, and the aggregate vercel-token detector is not attributed to this family.

families.name: App access token
families.description: Modern Vercel App access token identified by the provider-documented vca_ marker.
families.note: Product #858 records this semantic contract as pending/T0. The class and vca_ marker are provider-backed, but one opaque example does not establish a universal body grammar or boundary. No scored fixture/profile cells exist, and the aggregate vercel-token detector is not attributed to this family.

families.name: App refresh token
families.description: Modern Vercel App refresh token identified by the provider-documented vcr_ marker.
families.note: Product #858 records this semantic contract as pending/T0. The class and vcr_ marker are provider-backed, but the documentation reuses the app-access example body and establishes no universal body grammar or boundary. No scored fixture/profile cells exist, and the aggregate vercel-token detector is not attributed to this family.

families.name: API key
families.description: Modern Vercel API key identified by the provider-documented vck_ marker.
families.note: Product #858 records this semantic contract as pending/T0. The class and vck_ marker are provider-backed, but no reviewed source establishes a complete body grammar or boundary. No scored fixture/profile cells exist, and the aggregate vercel-token detector is not attributed to this family.

families.name: Granular access token
families.description: 2021-09 format token with a Base62 CRC32 checksum, prefixed npm_.

families.name: Legacy token
families.description: Pre-2021 unprefixed UUID-format token.
families.note: npm-token's own provider source is the changelog announcing the npm_ prefix scheme as a replacement, implying the prior UUID-format token predates it; that legacy shape is not matched by the npm_-prefixed pattern.

families.name: Generic API key
families.description: AIza prefixed general-purpose API key.

families.name: OAuth2 credential
families.description: OAuth2 client secret, access token or refresh token.
families.note: google-api-key's contract review notes the pinned TruffleHog detectors separately cover Gemini and OAuth2 credentials, not this generic AIza API-key shape.

families.name: API key
families.description: SG. prefixed API key (full-access and restricted-access permission scopes share this format).

families.name: Application client secret
families.description: Client secret value for an app registration, with a digit+Q~ marker.

families.name: Personal access token
families.description: 84-character PAT with a fixed AZDO signature at positions 76-80.

families.name: Legacy integration token
families.description: secret_ prefixed integration token.

families.name: Integration token
families.description: ntn_ prefixed integration token from Notion's 2024-09 rollout.
families.note: notion-token's contract review states this current ntn_-prefixed format has no contract here; the pinned gitleaks rule targets it instead of the legacy secret_ shape. Measured as the Beta.8 arrival family notion-integration-token (#211, research #225), separate from notion:legacy-integration-token: the ntn_ prefix is provider-documented, the 11-digit + 35-character body is tool-only and provisional, and PAT/OAuth/org-bot roles that may share the prefix are not merged into it.

families.description: ATAT prefixed API token (minimum-length contract; Atlassian disclaims a fixed length).

families.note: atlassian-api-token's contract review states the pinned TruffleHog detector targets the distinct ATCT access-token family, not the ATAT-prefixed API-token shape.

families.note: redact-secret#671 (product PR #679) split the legacy bare-hex generation into datadog:application-key-legacy; this family keeps the ddapp_ shape only.

families.name: Application key (legacy 40-hex)
families.description: Pre-ddapp_ 40-character lowercase-hex application key, still accepted by Datadog; recognized only beside a same-line DD_APPLICATION_KEY / datadog marker.
families.note: redact-secret#671 (product PR #679). Scored as policy (no value grammar), like datadog:api-key.

families.description: glc_ prefixed Cloud access policy token.

families.description: NRAK- prefixed user API key.

families.name: Legacy FCM server key
families.description: Legacy Firebase Cloud Messaging HTTP/XMPP server key: literal AAAA prefix, 7 bytes, a literal ":", then 140 bytes.
families.note: #81 backfilled the firebase-server-key detector (redact-secret#543). Service-account JSON exports and AIza-prefixed keys are covered elsewhere (private-key, google-api-key), not this family.

families.name: PEM-encoded private key
families.description: RFC 7468 textual encoding of private key material (any algorithm), not tied to a single provider.

families.name: JSON Web Token
families.description: RFC 7519 compact-serialization token, not tied to a single issuer.

families.description: RFC 6750 Authorization: Bearer value; a transport scheme, not a provider-specific format.

families.description: Base32 secret parameter of an otpauth:// key URI.

families.name: Unclassified assignment literal

families.name: Personal access token
families.description: dapi-prefixed 32-hex personal access token, optionally suffixed -<digit> after rotation.
families.note: redact-secret#308 (product PR #665) landed on the product main after 0.1.0-beta.6; the pinned published package predates it. OAuth client secrets are a separately documented scope extension, not this family.

families.name: Cloud API secret (cflt-prefixed)
families.description: API secret created after 2025-07-30: literal cflt prefix, then 54 base64-alphabet body bytes and a 6-byte checksum (standard Base64 of the little-endian CRC32 of those 54 bytes), 64 in total.
families.note: redact-secret#309 (product PR #667) landed on the product main after 0.1.0-beta.6 and checks the prefix and length only. #209 (research #234): the provider publishes the checksum algorithm, so the contract validates it. The API key ID ("not considered secret information") is never a positive.

families.name: Cloud API secret (unprefixed, pre-2025-07-30)
families.description: Unprefixed 64-byte base64-body API secret, recognized only beside a same-line confluent keyword.
families.note: redact-secret#309 (product PR #667). Scored as policy (no value grammar), like twilio:auth-token.

families.name: API key
families.description: PMAK-prefixed API key: 24 hex bytes, a literal "-", then 34 hex bytes (59-byte body); sent in the X-API-Key header.
families.note: redact-secret#310 (product PR #668) landed on the product main after 0.1.0-beta.6; the pinned published package predates it. The provider page documents only the header, so the grammar is tool-corroborated (T2).

families.name: Collection access key
families.description: PMAT- followed by 26 characters; a read-only key for one collection's JSON, shared through the collection URL's access_key parameter.
families.note: Registry detector postman-collection-access-key since redact-secret#700 (#773, registry pinned at 3144bb3), authored under #259. Postman documents the credential but no shape; the 26-character uppercase alphanumeric body follows GitLab's rule (T2).

families.name: Personal access token
families.description: nfp_-prefixed personal access token: 36 bytes of [A-Za-z0-9_], 40 characters total.
families.note: redact-secret#311 (product PR #666) landed on the product main after 0.1.0-beta.6; the pinned published package predates it.

families.name: CLI, OAuth, app and build tokens (nfc_/nfo_/nfu_/nfb_)
families.description: The announcement's four other nf-prefixed token classes, sharing the personal access token's scheme but issued for the CLI, OAuth flows, app.netlify.com and builds.
families.note: Out of redact-secret#311's explicit scope; each is a distinct credential, so none is a control or positive for netlify:personal-access-token.

families.name: OAuth access token (HRKU-prefixed)
families.description: HRKU- prefixed OAuth access token in its two documented prefixed generations: 41 characters (HRKU- plus a UUID, granted 2024-04-01 to 2025-04-22) and 65 characters (HRKU- plus 60 of [A-Za-z0-9_-], granted from 2025-04-23, observed to begin AA).
families.note: redact-secret#312 (product PR #675) landed on the product main after 0.1.0-beta.6 and froze the 65-character HRKU-AA grammar only. #209 (research #235): changelog-items/3175 documents the 41-character HRKU-<uuid> generation as the previous length, so it is in this family's contract, not an undocumented-width variant; the AA start of the 65-character form is example- and tool-observed, not provider-stated. The pre-2024 bare-UUID generation is heroku:legacy-api-key.

families.name: Legacy API key (bare UUID)
families.description: Pre-2024-04 unprefixed 8-4-4-4-12 hex UUID token, still valid until regenerated; recognized only beside a same-line heroku keyword.
families.note: redact-secret#312 (product PR #675). Scored as policy (no value grammar), like twilio:auth-token. The later HRKU-<uuid> (41 characters) and HRKU-AA (65) generations are provider-documented and belong to heroku:oauth-access-token (#209, #232). An app id on a heroku-named line is a public-id control; both keyword-gated peers flag it, and the product has excluded identifier-shaped keys since redact-secret#714.

families.name: Marketing API key
families.description: 32-hex API key followed by a literal -us and a one- or two-digit data-center number; recognized only beside a same-line mailchimp keyword.
families.note: redact-secret#313 (product PR #678) landed on the product main after 0.1.0-beta.6; the pinned published package predates it. Mandrill (transactional) keys are a separate product and not this family.

families.name: Private API key and HTTP webhook signing key
families.description: key- followed by 32 lowercase alphanumeric bytes; Mailgun's current API reference shows the same shape for the account HTTP signing key. Recognized only beside a same-line mailgun keyword.
families.note: redact-secret#314 (product PR #680) landed on the product main after 0.1.0-beta.6; the pinned published package predates it. One detector covers both credentials because the provider's current interface gives them one shape.

families.name: Public validation key (pubkey-)
families.description: pubkey- followed by 32 bytes; Mailgun's public email-validation key, not a secret.
families.note: Documented public per redact-secret#314's scope; gitleaks 8.30.1's mailgun-pub-key rule still flags it, which the mailgun-api-key public-id control records.

families.name: Prefix-less 32-8-8 hex key triplet
families.description: Dash-segmented 32-8-8 lowercase hex triplet that both pinned tools match and three sources describe as the newer private API key; recognized only beside a same-line mailgun keyword.
families.note: Beta.8 context-gated arrival family mailgun-api-key-triplet (#259). Since redact-secret#701 (#773, registry pinned at 3144bb3) the product mailgun-api-key detector also reports this shape under mailgun_api_key, inside the shared detector. It is no longer treated as a superseded legacy signing key: no issued key has been observed and the role is recorded uncertainty.

families.name: Management API token (SSWS)
families.description: 00-prefixed 42-character API token sent as Authorization: SSWS; recognized beside the SSWS scheme or a same-line okta keyword.
families.note: redact-secret#315 (product PR #681) landed on the product main after 0.1.0-beta.6; the pinned published package predates it. OAuth access/ID tokens are JWTs and belong to the jwt family, not this one.

families.name: API token
families.description: r8_ prefixed API token; the provider documents a 40-character total (a 37-character body) and does not state the body alphabet.
families.note: Registry detector replicate-api-token since redact-secret#727 (registry pinned at dad7868); graduated from a Beta.8 arrival family (#208, research #217), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/208.ts. The body alphabet is peer-contested (TruffleHog admits - and _; flare-redact alphanumeric only) and stays provisional. The cog/r8.im login token's relation to this token is undocumented and not claimed.

families.name: API key
families.description: gsk_ prefixed API key; the 52-character alphanumeric body is tool-corroborated, not provider-stated.
families.note: Registry detector groq-api-key since redact-secret#727 (registry pinned at dad7868); graduated from a Beta.8 arrival family (#208, research #218), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/208.ts. The observed WGdyb3FY body segment is a four-sample maintainer observation recorded as unresolved, not a grammar requirement; the community 48-character body proposal is unsupported. Not Grok/xAI.

families.name: API key
families.description: xai- prefixed API key; the 80-character body is documented only by the provider's example and corroborated by tools.
families.note: Registry detector xai-api-key since redact-secret#727 (registry pinned at dad7868); graduated from a Beta.8 arrival family (#208, research #216), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/208.ts. Management keys (tool-reported xai-token- prefix, XAI_MANAGEMENT_KEY) are a separate credential and not members of this family; no taxonomy family is added for them until the provider documents a format.

families.name: Inference API key
families.description: sk-or-v1- followed by 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters (73 characters), per OpenRouter's secret-format documentation.
families.note: Registry detector openrouter-api-key since redact-secret#727 (registry pinned at dad7868); graduated from a Beta.8 arrival family (#208, research #220), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/208.ts. Management keys (sk-or-mgmt-) are openrouter:management-api-key, not members of this family. The public key hash has the same 64-hex body shape without the prefix.

families.name: Management API key
families.description: sk-or-mgmt- prefixed management (formerly provisioning) key for the /api/v1/keys routes; cannot call completion endpoints. Body length and alphabet are undocumented.
families.note: Unsupported and unclaimed (#208, research #220): a real secret, but no body grammar is published and no product detector, contract or fixture targets it. It is never used as a benign control of openrouter:api-key.

families.name: API key (personal access token or service key)
families.description: LangSmith API key in its two documented roles, personal access token (lsv2_pt_) and workspace/org service key (lsv2_sk_); the 32+10 lowercase-hex segment grammar is tool-corroborated.
families.note: Registry detector langsmith-api-key since redact-secret#728 (registry pinned at dad7868); graduated from a Beta.8 arrival family (#210, research #219), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/210.ts. Legacy ls__ keys, license keys, SCIM tokens, OAuth tokens and deployment keys are separate credentials this family does not claim.

families.name: Secret API key
families.description: Langfuse project/organization secret key as the issuer mints it: sk-lf- plus a lowercase UUIDv4 (42 characters). Paired with the public pk-lf- key.
families.note: Registry detector langfuse-secret-key since redact-secret#728 (registry pinned at dad7868); graduated from a Beta.8 arrival family (#210, research #221), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/210.ts. Self-hosted operator-defined values and a possible sk-lf-gw- gateway shape are recorded but not claimed.

families.name: API key
families.description: pplx--prefixed API key; the 48-character alphanumeric body is tool-corroborated, not provider-stated.
families.note: Registry detector perplexity-api-key since redact-secret#730 (registry pinned at f2082ab); graduated from a Beta.8 arrival family (#212, research #226), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/212.ts.

families.name: API key
families.description: fw_-prefixed API key; 22- and 24-character bodies are observed, not documented.
families.note: Registry detector fireworks-ai-api-key since redact-secret#730 (registry pinned at f2082ab); graduated from a Beta.8 arrival family (#212, research #227), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/212.ts. The fpk_ Fire Pass key and any unprefixed legacy key are not covered.

families.name: API key (pcsk_)
families.description: Current pcsk_<label>_<secret> API key; prefix from provider code, segment widths tool-corroborated.
families.note: Registry detector pinecone-api-key since redact-secret#730 (registry pinned at f2082ab); graduated from a Beta.8 arrival family (#212, research #228), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/212.ts. The Admin API docs describe an unobserved pckey_ prefix; that contradiction is unresolved.

families.name: Legacy API key (bare UUID)
families.description: Legacy bare-UUID API key, identical in shape to Pinecone key/project/service-account ids; recognized only beside a same-line Pinecone API-key identifier.
families.note: Beta.8 context-gated arrival family pinecone-api-key-legacy (#212, research #228); the UUID shape is corroborated by unpinned tools only. Owned by the product pinecone-api-key detector since product main 2420e80 (redact-secret#766 and its ADR 2026-09-24-claim-a-legacy-pinecone-uuid-key-only-under-its-api-key-name): the UUID is redacted at high confidence under a Pinecone API-key name (PINECONE_API_KEY, pinecone_api_key, PINECONE_KEY, or api_key/apiKey/Api-Key on a line naming pinecone), and a bare UUID stays unclaimed. The detector reports it with the same pinecone_api_key finding type as pcsk_, so detectors stays empty: mapping the family to pinecone-api-key would merge it into that contract (#253).

families.name: Runner authentication token
families.description: glrt--prefixed runner authentication token: a 20-character legacy body, or the routable base64url payload with a base36 length holder and CRC32 checksum.
families.note: Registry detector gitlab-runner-authentication-token since redact-secret#730 (registry pinned at f2082ab); graduated from a Beta.8 arrival family (#212, research #230), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/212.ts. glrtr-, instance-prefixed and unversioned routable variants are not claimed. gitlab-token contract covers glpat- only.

families.name: API token
families.description: 22-character alphanumeric API token sent in an Authorization: token header; recognized only beside a same-line travis keyword.
families.note: Registry detector travisci-api-token since redact-secret#523 (#773, registry pinned at 3144bb3), authored under #259. Travis CI states no shape; the 22-character grammar is tool-corroborated (gitleaks travisci-access-token, trufflehog travisci).

families.name: API key
families.description: napi_-prefixed API key (personal, organization or project-scoped); the 64-character alphanumeric body floor is tool-corroborated.
families.note: Registry detector neon-api-key since redact-secret#524 (#773, registry pinned at 3144bb3), authored under #259. The napi_ prefix is provider-documented; the body floor rests on betterleaks and mask-go (T2). Legacy unprefixed keys are not covered.

families.name: Enterprise organization key (sk-ant-api01-)
families.description: sk-ant-api01- prefixed key that Anthropic documents as a Compliance Access Key; the prefix is the general Claude Enterprise organization key for any scope set, so a finding must not claim 'compliance'.
families.note: Beta.10 arrival family anthropic-api01-key (#384, research redact-secret#776, product #862). The product extends the shared anthropic-token detector and keeps the anthropic_api_key type, so this family maps to no registry detector and shows the measured status of an unscored arrival id, never the status of anthropic:secret-api-key. T1 on the prefix only; the body is unspecified.

families.name: Admin API key (sk-ant-admin01-)
families.description: sk-ant-admin01- prefixed full-access Admin API key created by organization admins in the Claude Console.
families.note: Beta.10 arrival family anthropic-admin01-key (#384, research redact-secret#775, product #862). Same shared-detector reason as anthropic:compliance-access-key. T1 prefix, tool-corroborated 93-character + AA body.

families.name: Admin API key (sk-admin-)
families.description: sk-admin- prefixed organization admin key with the T3BlbkFJ marker between two 58- or 74-byte segments; a marker-less body is out of contract.
families.note: Beta.10 arrival family openai-admin-api-key (#384, research redact-secret#777, product #863). openai-token already recognises sk-admin-, but a taxonomy family mapped to it would borrow the status of openai:secret-api-key, so it is measured as its own unscored arrival id. T2.

families.name: Long-term API key (ABSK)
families.description: ABSK-prefixed standard-Base64 key for an IAM service-specific credential; its decoded form is BedrockAPIKey-<user>-at-<account>:<secret>.
families.note: Registry detector aws-bedrock-long-term-api-key since redact-secret#864 (registry pinned at cfe2aec); graduated from a Beta.10 arrival family (#384, research #778), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/384b.ts. T1 by maintainer ruling of 2026-09-27 (redact-secret#778): the ABSK prefix and standard-Base64 alphabet, from the AWS Security Blog scan pattern; lengths stay T2. Not the short-term key, the public IAM alias or an access key id.

families.name: Short-term API key (bedrock-api-key-)
families.description: bedrock-api-key- prefixed Base64 pre-signed CallWithBearerToken URL, valid for at most 12 hours.
families.note: Registry detector aws-bedrock-short-term-api-key since redact-secret#864 (registry pinned at cfe2aec); graduated from a Beta.10 arrival family (#384, research #779), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/384b.ts. T1 by maintainer ruling of 2026-09-27 (redact-secret#779): the bedrock-api-key- prefix, the fixed 133-character head and standard padded Base64, from AWS-authored token generators and the blog; total length stays T2. The product reports the two Bedrock keys as separate detectors.

families.name: API key (sk_)
families.description: sk_ + 48 lowercase hex, with an optional provider-code-evidenced _residency_<region> suffix, sent in the xi-api-key header.
families.note: Registry detector elevenlabs-api-key since redact-secret#865 (registry pinned at cfe2aec); graduated from a Beta.10 arrival family (#384, research #788), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/384c.ts. T1 by maintainer ruling of 2026-09-27 (redact-secret#788) on ElevenLabs SDK code for the sk_ prefix and the _residency_[a-z0-9]+ suffix grammar; the 48-lowercase-hex body stays T2 and no fixture asserts it. sk_ is shared with Stripe (sk_live_, sk_test_, sk_org_) and Pollinations.

families.name: Project API key (tgp_v1_)
families.description: tgp_v1_ + 43 base64url characters; a deprecated legacy key population has an undocumented format and is not claimed.
families.note: Registry detector together-ai-api-key since redact-secret#867 (registry pinned at cfe2aec); graduated from a Beta.10 arrival family (#384, research #783), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/384d.ts. T2; no pinned scanner has a Together rule (betterleaks only, a gitleaks lineage). The arrival id together-api-key was renamed to the detector id.

families.name: API key (tvly-)
families.description: tvly- with an optional dev- segment and a 32-character alphanumeric body; tvly-prod- and production key widths are unresolved.
families.note: Registry detector tavily-api-key since redact-secret#867 (registry pinned at cfe2aec); graduated from a Beta.10 arrival family (#384, research #786), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/384d.ts. T2; no pinned scanner has a Tavily rule (noseyparker and GitGuardian only).

families.name: Studio API key (unprefixed)
families.description: 32 alphanumeric characters recognised only beside a same-line Mistral name, host or SDK constructor; no prefix is documented.
families.note: Registry detector mistral-api-key since redact-secret#868 (registry pinned at cfe2aec); graduated from a Beta.10 arrival family (#384, research #781), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/384e.ts. T2, context-gated, no bare-value claim; generic coverage already redacts labelled forms, so the family adds the SDK-call-argument forms.

families.name: API key (unprefixed)
families.description: 40 alphanumeric characters recognised only beside a same-line cohere or CO_API_KEY name, host or SDK constructor; trial and production keys share one shape.
families.note: Registry detector cohere-api-key since redact-secret#868 (registry pinned at cfe2aec); graduated from a Beta.10 arrival family (#384, research #782), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/384e.ts. T2, context-gated, no bare-value claim.

families.name: API key (unprefixed)
families.description: 40 lowercase hex characters recognised only beside a same-line Deepgram name, host or SDK constructor; sent as Authorization: Token, not Bearer.
families.note: Registry detector deepgram-api-key since redact-secret#868 (registry pinned at cfe2aec); graduated from a Beta.10 arrival family (#384, research #789), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/384e.ts. T2, context-gated, no bare-value claim; the hex versus base36 alphabet is disputed between the tools and asserted by no fixture.

families.name: API key (unprefixed)
families.description: 32 alphanumeric characters recognised only beside a same-line AI21 name, host or SDK constructor; the shape rests on one ten-sample maintainer observation.
families.note: Registry detector ai21-api-key since redact-secret#868 (registry pinned at cfe2aec); graduated from a Beta.10 arrival family (#384, research #784), contract in benchmarks/lib/beta8/384e.ts. T0, context-gated: no provider statement and no scanner rule; pending.

families.name: API key (no evidenced shape)
families.description: No identifying prefix, length or alphabet is evidenced; only the key id, team id and user id are documented, as UUIDs.
families.note: Beta.10 context-gated arrival family exa-api-key (#384, research redact-secret#787, product #868). T0: measures the keyword gate and the SDK-call-argument forms only; no value grammar is claimed and none is fabricated.

families.name: Realtime client token (rt_)
families.description: Short-lived rt_ token that a server mints with a Studio API key (POST /v1/client/sessions) and a browser sends in the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header; the prefix and carrier are provider-documented, the body is not.
families.note: Beta.10 research disposition (redact-secret#780, benchmarks #384): pending, no corpus. No source states a body length, alphabet or checksum, so only a carrier-gated shape could be justified and it needs hands-on issuance first; keyed env and Bearer contexts are already redacted by generic paths, and the documented client_secret.value and WebSocket subprotocol carriers are a generic-carrier question, not a Mistral family. Not the Mistral Studio key (mistral:api-key).

families.name: API key (pa- or al-)
families.description: Voyage AI platform key (pa-) and MongoDB Atlas model API key (al-, al-eu-, al-us-); a 43-character [A-Za-z0-9_-] body rests on one scanner rule with no cited origin.
families.note: Beta.10 research disposition (redact-secret#785, benchmarks #384): pending, no corpus. The only body evidence is one betterleaks rule and community pages, no issued key confirms it, and pa- and al- are common two-letter prefixes, so a bare rule has low precision. Named-assignment, Bearer, JSON, YAML and tool-call forms are already redacted by the generic paths; revisit after the hands-on issuance the research comment lists.
